item.title: tuios
item.description:
The Problem Developers who need to run multiple interactive shells inside a single terminal often resort to tmux or screen. Those tools lack modern UI features such as mouse‑driven pane resizing, native graphics (kitty/sixel), and a modal, vim‑like command palette, forcing users to maintain separate scripts for layout automation.

item.title: TraceAnything
item.description:
The Problem
Videos are typically processed as sequences of independent frames or as static 3D reconstructions, which loses temporal continuity. Tracking arbitrary points across a video—whether for editing, 3D reconstruction, or scene understanding—requires either expensive per-frame correspondence matching or specialized trackers that don't generalize well. Trace Anything addresses this by representing an entire video as a continuous 4D trajectory field: each pixel maps to a parametric 3D traje...

Without an official app, users are stuck with the factory firmware's limited interface.

item.title: zero agent
item.description:

AI coding assistants typically operate as black boxes with opaque permission models and remote telemetry. Teams needing local, auditable code automation require control over which models handle their code, what operations are permitted (file writes, shell commands, network access), and durable session persistence without external dependency.

item.title: serie
item.description:

item.title: minichord
item.description:
The Problem
The Omnichord, a beloved electronic autoharp, was discontinued by Suzuki in 2015, leaving musicians with no affordable source for its distinctive chord strumming and harp sounds. Existing alternatives are either expensive vintage units, complex DIY builds, or software that fails to capture the tactile, playable feel of the original.

item.title: CLI Anything
item.description:
The Problem Many desktop and server applications expose only graphical or ad‑hoc command‑line interfaces, making them difficult for autonomous AI agents to invoke reliably. Engineers must write custom wrappers for each tool, duplicating effort and introducing brittle integrations.

item.title: LH Stinger
item.description:
The Problem
The LH-Stinger addresses the trade-off between speed and print quality in consumer FDM printers. Most Cartesian designs sacrifice rigidity for speed or use CoreXY kinematics that complicate belt paths and maintenance. This project targets users who want high-speed printing (400-600 mm/s) without the flimsy frame and complex motion systems typical of budget high-speed machines.
What This Does

item.description:

This opacity can lead to unexpected charges and difficulty budgeting for large codebases or CI pipelines.
